articles.title: A joke domain purchase turned in geopolitical warfare
articles.titleZh: 一个玩笑域名的购买演变成了地缘政治战争
articles.author: kareiva

review.argument: Argument: it claims that a hobbyist radiosonde tracking site accidentally became a geopolitical asset, and that its open data is now used by militaries and governments in ways the operators never intended, capped by the realization that they are now entangled in warfare.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a benign tool built for fun can be repurposed by powerful actors, and how the operators must navigate ethical and legal dilemmas; the reader gains a concrete sense of how open data can have unintended military applications. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one — that the site's reverse predictions inadvertently mapped artillery sites and that military use is now a routine part of their operations; delete the writer and you lose the narrative and the argument, not just a list of events.
review.appeal: +12 — it is about a real-world collision of hobbyism, open data, and war, with vivid scenes (the cheese fortune teller, the FAA asking about weather balloons, the AWS support email about loss of life) that make it readable cold and worth sharing.

zh.thesis: 一个用于追踪气象气球的业余网站，意外成了军事侦察的辅助工具，并卷入了地缘政治冲突。
paragraphs: 2018 年，作者注册了 sondehub.org，原本只是个玩笑——它只是重定向到 Habhub，一个追踪业余气球的网站。但后来气象气球的追踪需求越来越多，他们开始自己存储数据，并建立了自己的预测系统。
他们开发了一个「反向预测」功能，利用已经发射的气球数据反推发射地点。这本来是为了好玩，但意外发现，这能画出军事炮兵阵地的位置，甚至还能探测到海上的军船。
2023 年，美国击落了所谓的「中国间谍气球」，SondeHub 一夜爆红。之后，来自 .mil 和 .gov 的请求不断，还有航空管制塔的。但真正的麻烦在 2024 年底来了——有人开始频繁攻击他们的 API。
他们发现，攻击者是一个乌克兰的深打击团队，正在利用 SondeHub 的风预测数据来计算无人机航迹，以「冲浪」到目标区域。他们警告了这个团队，同时发布了本地运行的预测工具，并联系了 AWS，确保数据不会泄露发射地点。
2025 年，美国「战争部长办公室（情报与安全）」要求提供数据。由于没有社区利益，他们开了发票，但对方从未付款。他们也没被追究。
他们还收到过 NTSB 的询问，关于犹他州的气球与飞机相撞事件；还被 FAA 追问，因为气象气球的存在让他们很惊讶。还有一些奇怪的邮件，比如一个「奶酪占卜师」写的文章，以及一个认为气候变暖是骗局的瑞士公司。
所以，一个业余的气象气球追踪项目，现在成了军事和民用航空都要依赖的基础设施。这篇博客只是冰山一角，作者说可能还有第二部分。

en.thesis: An amateur weather balloon tracking site accidentally became a military reconnaissance aid and got drawn into geopolitical conflict.
paragraphs: In 2018 the author registered sondehub.org as a joke, a redirect to Habhub, a site for tracking amateur balloons. But as tracking weather balloons grew, they started storing the data themselves and built their own prediction system.
They developed a 'reverse prediction' feature that back-calculates launch sites from balloon data. It was for fun, but it turned out to map artillery locations and even spot military ships at sea.

In 2023, after the US shot down a so-called Chinese spy balloon, SondeHub went viral. Requests poured in from .mil and .gov addresses, and air traffic control towers. But the real trouble started in late 2024, when someone began hammering their API.

They found the attacker was a Ukrainian deep strike team using SondeHub's wind predictions to plot drone paths and 'surf' the sky to targets. They warned the team, published a local predictor, and contacted AWS to ensure data wouldn't leak launch sites.
In 2025 the US Office of the Secretary of War (Intelligence and Security) requested data. Seeing no community benefit, they invoiced them, but never got paid or followed up.

They also got queries from the NTSB about a balloon-plane collision in Utah, and from the FAA, surprised that weather balloons exist. There were oddballs too, like a 'cheese fortune teller' and a Swiss company that thinks climate change is a hoax.
So an amateur weather balloon tracking project has become infrastructure that militaries and civil aviation rely on. This post is only part of the story; the author hints at a part two.

articles.title: Pluralistic: The ordinariness of evil (19 Aug 2026)
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

review.argument: Argument: it claims that AI's destructive potential is being amplified by critics as 'criti-hype,' which inadvertently helps AI companies raise money, and argues that treating AI as ordinary rather than exceptional is the way to stop its harmful march.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how repeating a booster's claims as warnings can backfire, and the reader can apply this to any hype cycle, not just AI. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that criti-hype is counterproductive, not just the examples.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a technology that affects jobs and the economy, it has a hook (the idea that critics are helping the hype), and it is readable cold with vivid metaphors.

zh.thesis: AI 的破坏性潜能只是表面上的危险，真正的问题是它被当作赌注，而我们应该把它当作普通技术来对待。
paragraphs: AI 老板们不断公开渲染 AI 的破坏性未来，从取代工作到毁灭世界。但这听起来像是担忧，实际上是在吹嘘——因为这是他们唯一的卖点。
现有 AI 只是补充工具，像插件一样，只对能用它的人有价值。它不值得每年万亿的投资，也不值得各国公务员被大规模替换。
真正的破坏性在于：AI 销售员让你被解雇，数据中心泡沫让地方放弃环保审查，消耗能源和水，产生大量碳。这正是我们需要批评的。
我们还要停止帮他宣传。桑德斯不该说要拥有它们，而应说泡沫破裂时不会救助。别再提「AI 安全」或「流氓 AI」，而要问他们为什么连安全沙箱都建不好。
AI 是普通技术，不是魔法。它不会让你变邪恶，也不会让你发疯。就算 AI 公司破产，服务器卖个一折，用它们运行模型也不会被「污染」。
把 AI 说成特别邪恶，反而把那些平庸的骗子捧成超级恶棍。阿尔特曼是骗子，不是天才。我们帮他们融资，就是帮他们搞庞氏骗局。
正确的批评是指出他们在撒谎，而不是用「批评式炒作」重复他们的谎言。AI 是日常的，就像汽车一样，有好处也有坏处，我们要做的是限制坏处。

en.thesis: AI's destructive potential is the surface of the danger; the real problem is the bet on it, and we should treat AI as ordinary.
paragraphs: AI bosses keep publicly wringing their hands about AI's destructive future, from taking jobs to ending the world. It sounds like worry, but it's really boasting — because it's all they're selling.
Existing AI is a marginal tool, a plug-in, useful only to those who can use it. It doesn't warrant trillion-dollar yearly investment, or mass firings of civil servants replaced by chatbots.

The real destructiveness is here: salesmen getting you fired, data-center bubbles that make towns ditch environmental review, consuming water and energy, emitting carbon. That's what we should attack.

We should stop amplifying their narratives. Sanders shouldn't say the government should own half, but that there will be no bailout. Drop 'AI safety' and 'rogue AI'; instead ask why they can't build a secure sandbox for their hacking tools.

AI is a normal technology, not magic. It won't corrupt you or drive you mad. Even if the companies go bankrupt and servers sell at ten cents on the dollar, running open models on them won't infect you.
Treating AI as exceptionally evil elevates mediocre conmen to supervillain status. Altman is a fraud, not a genius. We help him raise money for his Ponzi scheme.
Right criticism is to point out they're lying, not to repeat their lies as warnings. AI is ordinary, like a car — useful and harmful, and we can restrict the harm.

articles.title: An LLM wiki changed how I work
articles.titleZh: LLM 维基如何改变了我的工作方式
articles.author: Casey Newton

review.argument: Argument: it claims that an LLM wiki—a self-organizing knowledge base built from personal archives and daily clippings—is the most useful productivity tool the author has adopted, and it details the setup, maintenance costs, and payoff. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a personal knowledge base can automate the curation of one's own past work and current interests, which is a concept any knowledge worker can apply to their own field. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that this specific workflow is worth the maintenance, not just a list of apps.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a tool that promises to change how people manage information, it includes concrete scenes of the author using it, and it has a hook: the idea that AI can write your wiki for you. Readable cold.

zh.thesis: 用 LLM 自动整理个人知识库能大幅提升工作效率，但需要持续维护。
paragraphs: 今年四月，知名 AI 研究者 Andrej Karpathy 发推介绍了一种方法：用 LLM 从本地文档中提取内容，自动生成并更新 Markdown 维基。这个想法迅速传开，我花了数周搭建，最终证明非常有用。
我的维基最初用自己写过的所有文章做种子，Claude 从中提取了人物、公司和概念，生成了上千个页面。比如 Meta 的页面超过 1.2 万字，链接了 1300 多个词条。
每天早晨，我用 Obsidian 的剪贴器保存新闻，脚本自动把它们并入维基。现在我有 1440 多个页面，涵盖了我关心的所有话题，还能通过插件直接提问。
在处理复杂新闻（如 OpenAI 智能体安全事件）时，我每天先查维基回顾脉络，再核对原始来源，省下大量时间。它还能自动生成新概念页面，为我提供选题灵感。
但维基需要频繁维护：页面过长要压缩，脚本出错要修，Claude 的写作风格太压缩，我用 GPT 重写了大部分内容。即使如此，我每天早晨都很期待看它生成的新内容。
这个系统可能太个人化，不便推荐给别人，但「自组织知识库」正是我从 2008 年用 Evernote 以来一直追求的方向。使用前沿工具的代价是来得太早，但回报是我乐在其中。

en.thesis: Using an LLM to auto-organize a personal knowledge base is a huge productivity win, but it requires constant upkeep.
paragraphs: In early April, prominent AI researcher Andrej Karpathy tweeted a method: use an LLM to extract content from local documents and auto-generate a Markdown wiki that updates as you add material. The idea spread fast, and I spent weeks building one. It has proven extremely useful.

I seeded my wiki with my own writing — the entire Platformer archive. Claude extracted people, companies, and concepts, generating thousands of pages. My Meta page runs over 12,000 words and links to 1,300 other wiki pages.
Each morning, I use Obsidian's web clipper to save stories, and a script merges them into the wiki. Now I have over 1,440 pages covering topics I care about, and I can query it with a simple plugin.

When covering a complex story like the OpenAI agentic breach, I check the wiki each day to refresh my memory, then verify against original sources. It saves me hours and also generates new concept pages, suggesting story ideas.

But the wiki needs constant maintenance: pages get too long, scripts break, and Claude's style is too compressed. I used GPT to rewrite much of it. Even so, I look forward to seeing what it builds each morning.

The system may be too personal to recommend widely, but a self-organizing knowledge base is the logical end of what I've wanted since Evernote in 2008. The cost of bleeding-edge tools is arriving early, but the payoff is enjoyment.

articles.title: What Happens If OpenAI Dies?
articles.titleZh: 如果 OpenAI 死了会怎样？
articles.author: Ed Zitron

review.argument: Argument: it claims OpenAI's economics are so ruinous that its collapse is a real possibility, and traces the specific obligations and funding gaps that make it so. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a company can make commitments so large that its survival depends on impossible growth, and the reader sees the same pattern in other hype cycles. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument, not just the numbers.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about money and jobs, it contradicts the prevailing narrative, and it is readable cold despite the jargon.

zh.thesis: OpenAI 因巨额支出和收入放缓，面临生存危机，其倒闭可能引发系统性风险。
paragraphs: OpenAI 的生存能力令人担忧。一周内完成 70 亿美元回购，同时 COO 和 CRO 离职，CRO 上任仅八个月。
OpenAI 2025 年营收 130.7 亿美元，亏损 209 亿美元。年化收入增长放缓，7 个月才从 250 亿增至 400 亿，而对手 Anthropic 已达 650 亿。
OpenAI 到 2030 年有超过 8000 亿美元的算力承诺，需要每年融资 1000 亿至 2000 亿。主要投资者如软银、亚马逊已现金紧张。
软银已质押全部 OpenAI 持股贷款，亚马逊投资后自由现金流转负，英伟达表示今年投资可能是最后一次。
若 Anthropic 先 IPO，其糟糕的财务将打击 OpenAI 上市前景。OpenAI 估值过高，难以吸引新投资者。
倒闭可能表现为：微软收购、任由死亡、或与 Anthropic 合并。但都难以解决根本问题。
OpenAI 的未来依赖于不可能：到 2030 年营收达 2840 亿美元并盈利。否则，其倒闭将冲击整个行业，甚至威胁软银。

en.thesis: OpenAI faces an existential crisis due to massive spending and slowing revenue, and its collapse could trigger systemic risks.
paragraphs: OpenAI's ability to survive is doubtful. In one week it completed a $7 billion buyback while its COO and CRO left, the latter after only eight months.

OpenAI lost $20.9 billion on $13.07 billion revenue in 2025. Its annualized revenue growth is slowing, taking seven months to go from $25 billion to $40 billion, while rival Anthropic has reached $65 billion.
OpenAI has over $800 billion in compute commitments by 2030, needing $100-200 billion in fresh capital every year. Major backers like SoftBank and Amazon are already cash-strapped.
SoftBank has pledged all its OpenAI holdings for a loan, Amazon's free cash flow has gone negative after investing, and Nvidia says this year's investment may be its last.
If Anthropic goes public first, its poor financials would hurt OpenAI's IPO prospects. OpenAI's valuation is too high to attract new investors.
A collapse could take the form of Microsoft absorbing it, being allowed to die, or merging with Anthropic. But none solve the underlying issues.
OpenAI's future hinges on the impossible: reaching $284 billion revenue and profitability by 2030. Otherwise, its collapse would impact the whole industry and even threaten SoftBank.

articles.title: Pluralistic: IP can't save you from AI (18 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: IP 救不了你免受 AI 的伤害
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

review.argument: Argument: it claims copyright cannot protect creative workers from AI because it grants rights without bargaining leverage, and uses the Spirit Airlines data sale to Google as evidence that property rights fail where labor and privacy rights are needed. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how legal rights without power become assets for the powerful, and the reader sees the same pattern in their own workplace or consumer life. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that copyright expansion is a trap, not just the news about Spirit.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about jobs, privacy, and a concrete bankruptcy sale that contradicts the assumption that copyright protects individuals, and it is readable cold.

zh.thesis: 版权无法保护创作者免受 AI 取代，劳动权利和隐私权利才是根本。
paragraphs: 你不必相信 AI 艺术有多好，也能看出资本押注 AI 的目的：替换掉各种岗位上的工人。作为创作者和工人，想保护自己的劳动利益，但很多同行认为扩大版权就能阻止 AI 训练，这是错误策略。
首先，禁止抓取、分析、发表分析结果，会误伤大量有益活动，比如 OED、搜索引擎、互联网档案馆。想制定一部只针对 AI 训练的法律极其困难，甚至不可能，而且版权的确从未给创作者带来真正的谈判筹码。
版权理论假设创作者像小企业主一样，靠独家授权与媒体公司讨价还价。可是多年来反垄断乏力，媒体行业高度集中，5 家出版社、4 家制片厂、3 家唱片公司、2 个应用商店，还有一家电子书巨头。版权越来越强，老板越来越富，创作者却越来越穷。
故事中最重要的例子：Spirit Airlines 破产时，把员工的电子邮件、日历、文件等数据卖给了 Google，用于 AI 训练。这些作品是职务作品，版权归公司，不是员工，所以员工毫无控制权。这就是版权无法保护隐私的生动证明。
解决之道是承认创作者是工人，争取劳动权利，比如行业性集体谈判。版权诉讼只是让 AI 公司在付钱给媒体老板还是科技老板之间做选择，并不会把钱装进创作者口袋。
所以，别指望版权能救你。真正该做的是停止假装自己是小企业，联合所有工人争取部门谈判，联合所有消费者争取隐私权。赢了这些，才有权做点什么，而不只是有权愤怒。

en.thesis: Copyright cannot protect creators from AI; labor and privacy rights are the real defense.
paragraphs: You don't have to believe AI art is any good to see what capital is betting on: AI replacing workers of every kind. As an artist and worker, you want to protect your labor interests, but many peers think expanding copyright will stop AI training. That is a losing strategy.

First, banning scraping, analysis, and publication would hurt many beneficial activities, like the OED, search engines, and the Internet Archive. Drafting a law that only targets AI training is extremely hard, maybe impossible. And copyright never really gave creators bargaining power.

Copyright theory assumes artists are small business owners who license rights to media companies. But weak antitrust enforcement has left publishing and entertainment highly concentrated: five publishers, four studios, three labels, two app stores, and one ebook giant. Copyright keeps expanding, bosses keep getting richer, and creators poorer.

The clearest example: when Spirit Airlines went bankrupt, its emails, calendars, and files were sold to Google for AI training. These were works made for hire, so copyright belonged to the company, not the employees. They had no say. That is copyright failing to protect privacy.

The fix is to see creators as workers and win labor rights, like sectoral bargaining. Copyright lawsuits just decide whether AI companies pay media bosses or tech bosses; they never put money in creators' pockets.

So don't expect copyright to save you. The real move is to stop pretending you're a small business, join all workers in demanding sectoral bargaining, and all consumers in demanding privacy rights. Win those, and you have the right to do something, not just to be angry.

articles.title: I Was Compelled to Revisit: Rory Kennedy on “Freefall: A Reckoning For Boeing”
articles.titleZh: 被驱使回去重新审视：罗里·肯尼迪谈《自由落体：波音的清算》
articles.author: Nell Minow

review.argument: Argument: it claims Boeing's shift to a profit-first model, rooted in the McDonnell Douglas merger and Jack Welch-style management, caused the 737 MAX crashes and ongoing safety failures, and that accountability has been avoided through legal and regulatory loopholes.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how corporate incentives and regulatory capture can override safety in any industry, and the reader sees a concrete example of how 'too big to fail' plays out in aviation.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that Boeing's problems are systemic and that CEOs should face prison, not just fines.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a company people fly on, includes vivid scenes like the whistleblower's death and the Senate hearing, and has a hook: a CEO making $100 million while planes fail.

zh.thesis: 罗里·肯尼迪的新纪录片揭露波音在737 MAX空难后仍以利润为先、缺乏人性，而高管和监管机构都未真正担责。
paragraphs: 罗里·肯尼迪曾拍过《波音： downfall》，聚焦两起737 MAX坠机，夺走346条生命。波音先是说是飞行员失误，后来才承认是飞机的MCAS系统（稳定飞行的机动特性增强系统）的错。
但她发现飞机复飞后事故不断：引擎掉落、机舱冒烟、轮子失灵，阿拉斯加航空甚至在空中被炸出个洞。她感到必须再回去拍续集，于是有了《自由落体》。
更揪心的是，吹哨人约翰·巴内特在作证期间离奇死亡，其他吹哨人纷纷向她透露内部的混乱。影片展示了工厂内部：质量管理被抛弃，取而代之的是奖金驱动的成本削减。
公司从未真正负起责任。CEO们坐拥亿万财富，却连受害者家属的电话都不打一个。对比1985年日航空难，社长高木养根亲自走遍全国向家属道歉，波音的做法令人心寒。
她呼吁换一个工程师背景的CEO，像鱼从头臭起一样，从头开始强调安全和卓越。司法部、FAA（联邦航空管理局）也应对失职者追责，甚至入狱，才能真正形成威慑。

en.thesis: Rory Kennedy's new documentary reveals a Boeing that still prioritizes profit over safety and humanity, with executives and regulators alike escaping real accountability.
paragraphs: Rory Kennedy's earlier film focused on two 737 MAX crashes that killed 346 people. Boeing first blamed pilot error, then admitted the fault lay with the MCAS system (a flight-stabilization feature) and the plane itself.

But she kept reading about incident after incident after the planes returned to the skies: engines falling off, smoke in the cabin, wheels failing, and an Alaska Air flight with a hole blown in its side. She felt compelled to revisit the story, and made this sequel.

More haunting was the suspicious death of whistleblower John Barnett while he was testifying. Other whistleblowers reached out, revealing chaos inside the factories, where quality control had been traded for bonus-driven cost-cutting.

The company never took real responsibility. Its CEOs have amassed vast wealth while many families have not even received a direct apology. Kennedy compares this to the 1985 JAL crash, whose president traveled across Japan to apologize in person.

She urges a CEO with an engineering background, one who leads from the top with a focus on excellence and safety. The Justice Department and FAA (Federal Aviation Administration) must hold the culpable to account, even with prison time, to truly deter future negligence.

articles.title: Arabic has four words for sadness. Philosophy explains why
articles.titleZh: 阿拉伯语有四个表示悲伤的词，哲学解释了原因
articles.author: Chereen Shurafa

review.argument: Argument: it claims Arabic's four sadness words encode distinct philosophical stances on grief, and that the language itself shapes how suffering is understood. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a culture's vocabulary carves emotional experience into different kinds of endurance, and the reader can apply it to any language they know. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that lexical distinctions are philosophical positions, not just a list of words.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a universal human experience, it contradicts the assumption that sadness is one thing, and it is readable cold with no background.

zh.thesis: 阿拉伯语中丰富的悲伤词汇并非多余，而是反映了对情感复杂性的细腻认知。
paragraphs: 阿拉伯语里有四个表示悲伤的词，每个都有细微差别。这常被当作语言丰富性的例子，但哲学视角认为，这其实体现了对情感本质的深刻理解。
语言不只是表达情感，也塑造我们如何理解情感。多个词汇让说话者能更精确地区分不同的悲伤状态，也认可了这类经验的多维度。
所以，词汇的丰富不是偶然，而是对人生经验的诚实承认。它提醒我们，情感本身很复杂，不该被一个笼统的词简化。

en.thesis: Arabic's multiple words for sadness reflect a nuanced understanding of emotional complexity, not redundancy.
paragraphs: Arabic has four words for sadness, each with its own shade of meaning. Often cited as an example of linguistic richness, philosophy suggests it also reveals a deep understanding of emotion's nature.

Language doesn't just express emotion; it shapes how we understand it. Multiple terms let speakers distinguish between different states of sorrow and acknowledge the many dimensions of such experiences.
So the abundance of words is not accidental but an honest recognition of life's complexity. It reminds us that feelings are intricate and shouldn't be flattened into a single term.

articles.title: If this is true, the hyperscalers are toast
articles.titleZh: 如果这是真的，超大云厂商要完蛋了
articles.author: Joachim Klement

review.argument: Argument: it claims SLMs on local devices can replace 70-80% of LLM tasks, making hyperscaler data centre capex a bad investment, and cites a Stanford study with win/tie ratios and cost savings. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a cheaper, local alternative can disrupt a capital-intensive incumbent, and the reader can apply it to other tech shifts. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that data centres are the wrong bet, not just the study's numbers.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about money and the future of AI, has a startling stat (98.6% win/tie in chat), and is readable cold, though it leans on charts the reader can't see.

zh.thesis: 斯坦福的研究表明，小模型在绝大多数任务上已不输大模型，且成本低得多，数据中心的投资可能白费。
paragraphs: 斯坦福五月发表的研究对比了小语言模型和大语言模型。这里的小模型指能跑在本地电脑或手机上的模型，大模型则指数据中心里跑的。
他们让这些模型做聊天和推理任务，比较谁的回答更好。结果在聊天任务上，最好的小模型在 98.6% 的情况下不输大模型。
推理任务上小模型也追得很快，成功率从 2023 年的 50% 左右，提高到 2025 年 10 月的最难任务 51.5%，简单任务已接近 99%。
更关键的是成本：小模型的能耗和算力开销比大模型低 50% 到 85%，单位推理效率高出七倍。这让本地处理比云端便宜得多。
所以作者认为，四个用例里三个都能用本地模型替代，数据中心的投资可能打了水漂。真正的赢家或许是做台式机的戴尔和苹果。

en.thesis: A Stanford study suggests small models now match large ones on most tasks at far lower cost, making data-center investment questionable.
paragraphs: A Stanford study from May compared small language models with large ones. Small models run on a local computer or phone; large ones run in data centers.
They tested both on chat and reasoning tasks. On chat, the best small model matched or beat the large model in 98.6% of cases.
On reasoning, small models are catching up fast: success rates rose from around 50% in 2023 to 51.5% on the hardest tasks and near 99% on the easiest by October 2025.
The bigger point is cost: small models use 50-85% less energy and compute, and are seven times more efficient per watt. So local inference is cheaper than sending data to a data center.
The author concludes that three out of four use cases can move to local models, making data-center investments wasteful. The real winners may be desktop makers like Dell and Apple.

articles.title: Why I'm Staying Out Of The Substack Religion Debate
articles.titleZh: 为什么我不参加 Substack 上的宗教辩论
articles.author: Scott Alexander

review.argument: Argument: it claims that theism's 'divine simplicity' defense is a sleight of hand that subtracts limits rather than complexity, and that theism must face the same preemptive penalty as alien-conspiracy explanations. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a 'powerful hidden entity' explanation can be optimized to evade all standard debunking, and the reader can apply this to any conspiracy theory or supernatural claim. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument, not just the citations.
review.appeal: +8 — it has a vivid hook (the Napoleon-aliens analogy), a concrete target (Adelstein's argument), and a memorable reframing of 'simplicity' that a generalist can repeat at dinner.

zh.thesis: 无神论对我来说是一种直觉，先于任何论证，所以我没法再对神学辩论提起兴趣。
paragraphs: 最近 Substack 上又热闹起来，好几个作者在争论上帝是否存在。这让我想起 2000 年代初的在线无神论辩论，我以为那是时代产物，没想到它又回来了。不过这次我提不起劲。
我的无神论感觉像是先于这些论证的。就像我们不会认真讨论「外星人帮拿破仑崛起」一样，有些假设从一开始就被常识排除，而不是靠逐步的贝叶斯计算。
当然这很危险，容易变成「你的宗教和相信外星人一样蠢」的侮辱，也容易沦为荒谬感启发式。但为什么我们排除拿破仑场景？因为它过拟合：任何事都能用「有个强大的隐藏实体想促成这件事」来解释。
这种解释比真实解释还强，能绕过一切反驳。所以我们给它一个预防性惩罚，通常叫「阴谋论」。但外星人版本更棘手，因为不受人类限制，证据也更难找。
所有文化都用这种方式解释过未知：雷是雷神，太阳是太阳神。随着科学进步，这种解释被一个个丢弃，剩下的异常就是宇宙存在、意识、微调等。当有人用「强大实体」来解释这些时，我还没听就翻白眼了。
有人会说上帝是无限简单的存在，所以不受惩罚。但这是把「减少限制」当简化，你减掉的其实是「能力」这种正面属性，实际是在添加。如果这技巧成立，造星舰就该比造双翼机容易。
而且计算并不神秘，大脑损伤、药物、基因都影响它，AI 也没用到什么奇异基质。所以就算意识有奇异基质，也买不来无限计算。神学论证撑不住这个惩罚，于是我的感觉是：它本应一开始就被排除，这让我对辩论失去了兴趣。

en.thesis: My atheism rests on an intuition that precedes any argument, so I cannot get excited about theology debates anymore.
paragraphs: Lately Substack has been buzzing with authors debating whether God exists. It reminds me of the early-2000s online atheism scene, which I thought was a relic of its time. It is back, but I find it hard to care.

My lack of belief feels like it precedes these arguments. Just as we never seriously debate whether aliens helped Napoleon rise, some hypotheses are excluded by common sense from the start, not by careful Bayesian reasoning.

That is dangerous, of course, easily sliding into mockery or the absurdity heuristic. But why do we rule out the Napoleon scenario? Because it overfits: anything can be explained by 'a powerful hidden entity wanted that specific thing to happen.'

That kind of explanation beats real ones, plowing through any objection. So we give it a preemptive penalty, usually called a conspiracy theory. But the alien version is worse, because aliens aren't bound by human limits and are even harder to disprove.

Every culture has used this move: thunder is the storm god, the sun is a god. Science kept shrinking the anomalies, and now a few remain: existence, consciousness, fine-tuning. When someone explains them with a powerful entity, I roll my eyes before hearing the argument.

Some say God is infinitely simple, so the penalty doesn't apply. But that is a sleight of hand: subtracting 'limits' means adding capabilities. If it worked, building a starship would be easier than a biplane.

And computation is not mysterious: brain damage, drugs, genes all affect it, and AI does fine without exotic substrates. So even if consciousness had one, it wouldn't buy infinite computing. Theism can't bear the penalty, and so my feeling is that it should have been ruled out from the start, which is why I stay out of the debate.

articles.title: Why You Move Factors in to Whether It Protects You From Dementia
articles.titleZh: 为什么「怎么动」比「动不动」更能预防痴呆
articles.author: Jake Currie

review.argument: Argument: it claims the protective effect of physical activity on dementia depends on context, with leisure activity reducing risk and occupational activity increasing it, and cites a new meta-review of 4.2 million adults. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is that the same behavior can have opposite health effects depending on context, which applies to how the reader thinks about work vs. leisure in their own life. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that context matters, not just the study summary.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a health risk people live with, it contradicts the common assumption that all movement is good, and it is readable cold with a clear hook.

zh.thesis: 运动能否预防痴呆，取决于它是休闲活动还是体力工作，前者降低风险，后者反而升高。
paragraphs: 我们早就知道，规律运动能降低痴呆风险。但《柳叶刀·公共卫生》刚发表的一项大型综述发现，这个关联有个关键前提——活动的性质很重要。
研究人员汇总了 420 多万成年人的数据，发现闲暇时的运动（跑步、骑车、打球）能把痴呆风险降低 24%，而体力要求高的工作却让风险升高 20%。
这就是「体力活动悖论」，以前在心血管疾病上见过，现在延伸到了痴呆。为什么？休闲运动通常让人放松，还能减少压力、增加社交，而体力工作往往重复、休息少，还暴露于噪音和空气污染。
当然，观察性研究还不能下结论。但结合上月另一项研究——坐着时动脑（比如居家办公）比被动看电视时大脑区域更饱满——只能说，无论动还是不动，情境才是关键。

en.thesis: Whether exercise protects against dementia depends on its context: leisure activity lowers risk, but physically demanding jobs raise it.
paragraphs: We have long known that regular exercise is linked to a lower risk of dementia. But a new meta-review in The Lancet Public Health finds a key caveat: the context of the activity matters.

Pooling data from over 4.2 million adults, researchers found that leisure-time exercise (running, cycling, sports) cut dementia risk by 24 percent, while physically demanding jobs raised it by 20 percent.

This is the 'physical activity paradox,' already known for heart disease and now extended to dementia. Why? Leisure activity is usually relaxing, cuts stress, and often involves socializing, whereas hard jobs tend to be repetitive, allow little recovery, and expose workers to noise and air pollution.

Of course, this observational study can't prove causation. But combined with last month's finding that sitting while mentally active (like working from a desk) leaves bigger brain regions than passively watching TV, the takeaway is that context rules, whether you're moving or not.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Text Watermarking Proves AI Companies Do Not Care at All About Writing
articles.titleZh: Anthropic 的文本水印证明 AI 公司根本不在乎写作
articles.author: Jason Koebler

review.argument: Argument: it claims Anthropic's watermarking scheme reveals the company treats words as fungible and writing as a probabilistic game, and it grounds that claim in Anthropic's own blog post and the SynthID study's quality metrics. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a tech company's engineering mindset flattens a human craft into interchangeable tokens, and the reader sees the same logic in other AI products. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that synonym choice carries meaning and that thumbs-up rates are a poor proxy for writing quality.
review.appeal: +10 — it is about a tool millions use, it contradicts the company's assurance that quality is unaffected, and the writer's personal reflection on why he chooses words makes it readable cold.

zh.thesis: AI 公司把词语当作可互换的随机选择，这暴露了它们对写作这门手艺的漠视。
paragraphs: Anthropic 宣布未来的 Claude 会在文本里加入水印，帮助识别 AI 生成的内容。它不添加隐藏字符，也不改元数据，而是改动 AI 选词的方式。
具体来说，水印改变了选词时随机数的来源。在某些词的选择上，Anthropic 认为是「低风险」的，比如「grey」和「overcast」都形容阴沉，随便选哪个都不影响意思。
但任何写过东西的人都知道，这两个词并非永远等价。作者选哪一个，可能和风格、情绪、上下文有关，甚至是童年某个老师的用词习惯。Anthropic 却把它们视为可互换，用统计方法「推一下」水印。
Anthropic 声称水印不影响输出质量。它引用的 Google 研究用点赞量来评价质量，用户对水印和未水印的回复点赞率只差 0.01%。但这测的是满意度，不是写作水准。
作者真正的愤怒在于：AI 公司把写作当成概率游戏，词语是随机数生成器的产物，没有意识、没有决策。这正是 AI 文本显得空洞的原因。
所以，这件事的意义超越了水印本身。Anthropic 连宣布水印时都如此漫不经心，说明它根本不在乎写作这门手艺，只把词语当作可以随意摆布的棋子。

en.thesis: AI companies treat words as interchangeable random choices, which reveals their indifference to the craft of writing.
paragraphs: Anthropic has announced that future versions of Claude will watermark the text they generate, to help identify AI-written content. It adds no hidden characters and touches no metadata — instead it changes the way the model picks its words.

Specifically, the watermark changes the source of the randomness behind word selection. In certain choices Anthropic calls “low-stakes” — say, between “grey” and “overcast” to describe a dull sky — either word works, so the system can nudge the pick one way or the other to embed a pattern.

But anyone who has written anything knows these words are not always interchangeable. Which one an author chooses can come down to style, mood, context, or a phrase picked up from a third-grade teacher. Anthropic treats them as fungible and nudges them for its own purposes.

Anthropic insists the watermark does not affect output quality. It cites Google research that used thumbs-up rates to judge quality, finding only a 0.01% difference between watermarked and unwatermarked responses. But that measures user satisfaction, not literary merit.

The real grievance, the author argues, is that AI companies treat writing as a probabilistic game. The word choice is the product of a random number generator, with no consciousness or decision behind it. That is why AI text feels hollow.
So the significance here goes beyond the watermark itself. The casual way Anthropic announced it shows the company does not care about writing as a craft — it sees words as buttons to be pushed.

articles.title: The Wonders of the Male Human Pelvis
articles.titleZh: 男性人类骨盆的奇妙之处
articles.author: Jake Currie

review.argument: Argument: it claims the male human pelvis has a unique forward-oriented hip socket configuration that improves walking efficiency, and contrasts it with the female pelvis constrained by childbirth. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how evolutionary trade-offs shape bodies differently, and the reader can apply it to thinking about sex differences and adaptation. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument, not just the study summary.
review.appeal: +8 — it is about the reader's own body, has a hook (male pelvis overlooked), and is readable cold, though it stays at a distance.

zh.thesis: 男性骨盆独特的结构是为了更高效的直立行走，而女性骨盆因分娩需求未能演化出这些特征。
paragraphs: 关于女性骨盆的研究很多，因为「产科困境」涉及分娩难、直立行走和脑容量等众多演化权衡。男性骨盆则相对被忽视，直到现在。
一项发表于《科学报告》的新研究分析了91个现代人骨盆和两个尼安德特人男性骨盆，发现现代男性骨盆的髋臼位置更靠前，是独特的演化适应，利于运动。
行走被称为一系列「受控的跌落」：重心失衡，然后迈腿接住自己。每步都压关节、耗能量。男性骨盆让股四头肌更好地吸收冲击并弹回身体，步态更节能，长途行走更有优势。
女性因分娩需求受限，没能发展出这些改良。但研究也有实际用途：理解行走机制的演化，有助生物力学、康复和伤病预防等领域的研究。

en.thesis: The male pelvis is uniquely adapted for efficient bipedal locomotion, while the female pelvis could not evolve these changes because of childbirth demands.
paragraphs: There is plenty of research on the female pelvis, for good reason: the 'obstetrical dilemma' ties together difficult childbirth, upright gait, and brain size. The male pelvis has been relatively overlooked until now.

A new study in Scientific Reports analyzed 91 modern human pelvises and two male Neanderthal pelvises, finding that the modern male pelvis has hip sockets oriented more forward. That configuration is a unique adaptation favoring locomotion.

Walking has been described as a series of controlled falls: you destabilize your center of gravity, then swing a leg forward to catch yourself. Each step stresses joints and costs energy. The male pelvis lets the quads absorb shock and spring the body back up, making the gait more energy-efficient, an advantage over long distances.

Female pelvises were constrained by childbirth and so did not develop these modifications. But the findings have practical use too: understanding the evolution of our walking mechanism can inform research in biomechanics, rehabilitation, and injury prevention.

articles.title: The Generalizability Problem, the Natural Field Experiments Answer
articles.titleZh: 可推广性的难题，自然现场实验来回答
articles.author: conversableeconomist

review.argument: Argument: it claims the generalizability problem in social science is best answered by natural field experiments, and uses Scared Straight's failure to show why lab or pilot results mislead. Not an announcement.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a result from one context can fail when scaled, and the reader learns to ask 'who was studied and how' about any policy claim. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the argument that systematic variation is the answer, not just a summary of List's work.
review.appeal: +8 — it is about why programs that work in one place fail in another, which touches education, crime, and policy, and the Scared Straight example is a hook you'd repeat.

zh.thesis: 自然现场实验让被试者不觉察自己在实验中，从而得到更可靠、更易推广的结论。
paragraphs: 社会科学有个老问题：小范围研究的结果，能不能推广到别处？比如某个学区的项目提高了成绩和毕业率，那别的学区呢？全州、全国、别的国家呢？答案可不好说。
John List 在《自然》上给出一个思路：做自然现场实验，就是设计研究时，不让参与者知道自己正在被研究。经典做法是「审计研究」——派出一批资历相似但种族不同的助手去租房、贷款、买车、求职，看对方反应。房东和雇主都蒙在鼓里。
这类实验得先过伦理审查，而且只能让不知情者做日常会做的事，不能施加压力或威胁。List 本人做过大量此类研究，比如测试不同募捐宣传的效果，或者故意丢钱包看归还率。他现在是沃尔玛的首席经济学家，团队正跟 6000 多家供应商做实验，看什么能最有效地促使他们减排。
这样一想，机会遍地都是：政府可以试验不同措辞的提醒信，零售商能试不同标签，网络公司试不同信息格式。关键是，我们可以把原本随意发生的「变化」变成有计划的「实验」，从中学习。从这个角度看，世界上的自然现场实验还远远不够。

en.thesis: Natural field experiments allow researchers to study behavior without subjects knowing they are part of a study, yielding more reliable and generalizable results.
paragraphs: The social sciences have an old problem: can results from a small study be generalized to other settings? A program in one school district may raise test scores and graduation rates. Will it work in another district, statewide, nationwide, or in other countries? There is no simple answer.

John List, writing in Nature, offers one approach: natural field experiments, where the design keeps participants unaware they are being studied. A classic form is the audit study: send out assistants with similar credentials but different races to rent apartments, get loans, buy cars, or apply for jobs, and see how they are treated. The landlords and employers never know.

Such studies must get ethics approval and only ask the unwitting participants to do what they would normally do, with no added stress or threat. List has run countless such experiments—testing how donors respond to different campaign messages, or dropping wallets in public places to see how many are returned. As Walmart's chief economist, his team is running field experiments with 6,000 suppliers on what most effectively cuts their carbon emissions.

Once you think this way, opportunities are everywhere: governments could test different wording on reminder letters, retailers different labels, online firms different information formats. The key is that systematic variation can replace haphazard variation, making the world a learning ground. By that view, we have far too few natural field experiments.

articles.title: ‘There are 1.5 sex scenes, and the food looks just fine’
articles.titleZh: 「有1.5场性爱戏，食物看起来还不错」
articles.author: Vittles

review.argument: Argument: it claims the film Tony fails to capture Bourdain's appetite and complexity, reducing his origin story to an anodyne coming-of-age tale, and contrasts it with the lusty, sensualist memoir.
review.transfer: Transfers — the mechanism is how a biopic flattens a larger-than-life figure into a generic template, and the reader recognizes this pattern in other adaptations. No cap.
review.claim: A claim, and a contestable one; delete the writer and you lose the critical judgment, not just a plot summary.
review.appeal: +5 — it has a hook (the witty opening line about sex scenes and food), but it is mostly about a film and a chef, which may not resonate with a generalist who hasn't seen the film or read the book.

zh.thesis: 电影《托尼》虽然改编自《厨房机密》，却回避了布尔丹的欲望与好奇，只拍成一个平庸的青春成长故事。
paragraphs: 《托尼》改编自安东尼·布尔丹的回忆录《厨房机密》，但导演马特·约翰逊没有拍布尔丹的胃口。电影讲的是1975年夏天，一个名叫托尼的中产少年在科德角追求女孩，被迫到海鲜店打工洗锅。
原书里布尔丹写自己初尝牡蛎，形容它是「闪闪发光、有点性意味的物体」。电影里也有1.5场性爱戏，食物看起来却还好，影片风格温和无害，与原作的贪欲和生命力相去甚远。
名人起源故事得在成名前埋下人格的种子。布尔丹的人格是好奇、性感、与人相处的天赋，而这些在电影里统统缺席。聚焦狭窄，故事就失去了广度、戏剧性和复杂性。
所以这部片不是关于布尔丹的，它只是借了他的名字，拍了一个谁都会有的夏天。想看真正的布尔丹，不如去读《厨房机密》或者看《未知之旅》。

en.thesis: The film 'Tony', though adapted from 'Kitchen Confidential', avoids Bourdain's appetite and curiosity, landing as a bland coming-of-age story.
paragraphs: Tony is adapted from Anthony Bourdain's memoir Kitchen Confidential, but director Matt Johnson doesn't film Bourdain's appetite. Instead, it's the summer of 1975, and a middle-class teen named Tony chases a girl in Provincetown, forced into a pot-washing job at a seafood shack.

In the book, Bourdain describes his first oyster as a 'glistening, vaguely sexual-looking object'. The film has 1.5 sex scenes and food that looks just fine — harmless and anodyne, a world away from the original's lust and life force.

Origin stories need to plant the seeds of a persona before it's formed. Bourdain's persona is curiosity, sexuality, a way with people — all deliberately absent here. The narrow focus flattens the story, losing breadth, drama, and complexity.
So this isn't really about Bourdain; it borrows his name for a summer anyone could have. For the real thing, read Kitchen Confidential or watch Parts Unknown.

articles.title: 我错过了多少泼天的富贵？

review.argument: Announcement: the author recounts a colleague's question about Nvidia financing GPU purchases and his own regret at not buying semiconductor funds earlier, capped with the aphorism that one cannot earn beyond one's cognition.
review.transfer: Transfers weakly — the idea that missed investment gains stem from delayed recognition is relatable, but the piece offers no mechanism or analysis, just a personal anecdote and a fund statistic.
review.claim: A list: the body is a brief exchange plus a comment thread where readers share their own missed opportunities; delete the writer and you lose only the prompt, not an argument.
review.appeal: +3 — the hook of 'missed fortunes' and the striking 363% fund gain might prompt a dinner mention, but the piece is thin and mostly self-congratulatory.

zh.thesis: 人挣不到认知以外的钱，错过英伟达和半导体基金的暴涨是因为认知晚了几年。
paragraphs: 同事问硅谷居士，怎么看英伟达帮客户融资买自家 GPU，感觉像左脚踩右脚，怕流动性撑不住。他说，黄仁勋和华尔街大佬比我们聪明，他们不担心，我们别杞人忧天。
但他承认，自己直到 2025 年秋天才意识到 AI 时代真来了，而黄仁勋三年前就该看到了。要是从 2022 年就重仓半导体基金 SMH，那该多好。
他说，人挣不到认知以外的钱，也守不住认知以外的财富。认知晚了几年，就错过了泼天的富贵。过去五年 SMH 涨了 363%。
评论里有人分享错过和抓住机会的故事。一位读者 2024 年才开户，把资金投进美股，如今有 30% 到 90% 的利润，感谢居士改变了投资理念。
也有人后悔没早买，还有人因为听信投资行职员的话错过了抄底机会。多数人表示都错过了好几拨，现在跟着居士定投，希望还来得及。
所以，重要的是提升认知，否则机会来了也抓不住。定投指数和长期投资，是普通人能把握的财富路径。

en.thesis: You cannot earn money beyond your cognition, and missing Nvidia and semiconductor fund gains was because cognition came late.
paragraphs: A colleague asked the author how he saw Nvidia helping clients finance purchases of its own GPUs, like stepping on his own feet, worried about liquidity. He said Jensen Huang and Wall Street are smarter than us; if they don't worry, we shouldn't.

But he admitted he only realized the AI era had truly arrived in fall 2025, while Jensen saw it three years earlier. If he had heavily bought semiconductor fund SMH from 2022, it would have been great.
He said you cannot earn money beyond your cognition, nor keep wealth beyond it. His cognition was a few years late, so he missed the great fortunes. SMH is up 363% over five years.

Commenters shared stories of missing and seizing opportunities. One reader opened an account in 2024, invested in US stocks, and now has 30% to 90% profits, thanking the author for changing his investment philosophy.
Others regretted not buying earlier, some missed a dip due to a bank clerk's advice. Many have missed several waves and are now following the author's dollar-cost averaging, hoping it's not too late.
So the key is to improve cognition, otherwise opportunities pass by. Regular investing and long-term holding are the wealth path ordinary people can grasp.
